cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD asks, “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” and then asks, “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” No secret place is left out. I once hid in the cookie jar and left a trail of crumbs, friends. Still, nothing hides from the LORD.
The answer is a dream. The LORD quotes the prophets: “I had a dream! I had a dream!” They say it while prophesying lies in His name. They say it twice, friends, like they're really selling it.

The answer is minds. The LORD calls them “…prophets of the delusion of their own minds?” That tells you where their message comes from, and it isn't from Him. Verse 32 adds, “It was not I who sent them or commanded them…”

The answer is True. The LORD says the prophets suppose the dreams they tell one another will make His people forget His name. He compares it to their fathers, who forgot His name through the worship of Baal, a false god. So these dreams are being passed around, friends, and He says what the prophets suppose they'll do.

The answer is truthfully. The LORD says, “Let the prophet who has a dream retell it, but let him who has My word speak it truthfully.” The one who has His word is the one to speak it truthfully, friends. Then He asks, “For what is straw compared to grain?”

The answer is that they steal them from one another. The LORD says He is against “…the prophets who steal from one another words they attribute to Me.” They lift words from each other, then say the words came from Him. I think that's what makes it worse, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “It was not I who sent them or commanded them…” He says it about those who prophesy false dreams and retell them. They aren't His messengers, friends, even if they say they are.

The answer is no benefit at all. The LORD says, “…they are of no benefit at all to these people…” Their reckless lies lead His people astray. Notice He doesn't say a little or some, friends. He says none.
The answer is forsake. The LORD tells Jeremiah the prophet what to say: “What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.” The question gets a hard answer. It's a heavy one, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says of anyone who claims, “This is the burden of the LORD…” that “I will punish that man and his household.” The household is named right there, friends. The text says it plainly.

The answer is “What has the LORD answered.” Each man is to say to his friend and to his brother, “What has the LORD answered?” or “What has the LORD spoken?” It's a good question, friends. It sends you back to what He actually said.

The answer is that they twist the words of the living God. The LORD says, “…each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God, the LORD of Hosts, our God.” He gives the reason Himself, friends. Then in verse 37 He says to ask the prophet, “What has the LORD answered you?”

The answer is that He will forget them and cast them out. The LORD says, “…therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence…” He says this to those who claimed it after He specifically told them not to. The text says it plainly, friends.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “…both you and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.” So the city is named along with the people. The text says it plainly, friends.
